primary_exploratory_claim: Spatial continuity is locally redundant but the taxonomic identity of individually sufficient continuity carriers turns over strongly among sites.

supported_descriptive.evidence: 48 site-carrier records comprise 32 species; 20 species occur as carriers at one site only; no species occurs at more than three sites.

supported_descriptive.claim: Most site pairs share no continuity carrier.
supported_descriptive.evidence: 18/120 site pairs share at least one carrier species; pairwise Jaccard median = 0 and mean = 0.0316.

supported_descriptive.claim: Many sites have depth of redundancy greater than one.
supported_descriptive.evidence: Median number of individually sufficient species per site = 2; range = 1-8.

supported_descriptive.claim: Richer sites deepen redundancy in absolute number without increasing the sufficient-species fraction.
supported_descriptive.evidence: Richness vs redundancy depth rho = 0.668; richness vs sufficient-species fraction rho = -0.159; median sufficient fraction = 0.477.

supported_descriptive.claim: Greater richness is not accompanied by stronger single-species dominance.

not_supported: carrier turnover causes temporal stability or insurance
continuity carriers are functionally equivalent in general
the carrier role is a conserved species trait
cross-site taxonomic turnover is unexpected given regional species-pool differences
post hoc rank associations are confirmatory
